title: Nechemiah HaAmsoni (tanna)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Akiva. As in the Jerusalem Talmud, [Berakhot ch. 9 halakha 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.5.10) and [Sotah ch. 5 halakha 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.5.5.7), they said that he served Rabbi Akiva for twenty-two years and learned from him that 'et' and 'gam' are amplifications, while 'akh' and 'rak' are limitations. He said to him: 'You shall fear the Lord your God' (et Hashem) — what does this include? He answered: Him and His Torah.[^1]

And we find in [Pesachim 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.22b.11), [Kiddushin 57](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.57a.1-2), [Bava Kamma 41](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.41b.7-8), and Bekhorot 6a: Shimon HaAmsoni, and some say Nehemiah HaAmsoni, would expound every 'et' in the Torah; when he reached 'You shall fear the Lord your God (et Hashem)' he withdrew. His students said to him: Rabbi, what will be with all the 'etim' you expounded? He said to them: Just as I received reward for the expounding, so I receive reward for the withdrawing — until Rabbi Akiva came and expounded, etc. Hyman infers from this that he was before Rabbi Akiva.[^2]

Hyman writes that he found in Dikdukei Soferim that it cites a manuscript in which the words “His disciples said to him: Rabbi…” are absent. He argues that, if so, this resolves the Bavli and the Yerushalmi: that he truly received all this from his teacher Rabbi Akiva, and only 'et Hashem' he did not know how to expound until he finally heard it from Rabbi Akiva, his teacher.

notes.text: Both Yerushalmi witnesses give twenty-two years serving Rabbi Akiva and the answer “Him and His Torah.” The Bavli parallels give the disciples’ question and Akiva’s later explanation. Hyman reports a manuscript without the disciples’ words and proposes a reconciliation.

Hyman cites Bekhorot 6a. The matching passage at [Bekhorot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.6b.4-5) names Shimon alone. [Heilprin’s Shimon entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3426&lang=en) also gives the Nehemiah alternative.
